---
framework: Root Cause Analysis
---

# Referral hand-off gaps

The clinic sends a referral to the district hospital, and from that moment the coordinator loses visibility into what happens next. Three consecutive months of records were pulled and the pattern is blunt: about a third of referrals never generate a hospital-side appointment at all, and nobody at either end owns the gap. The hospital intake desk says it never received a fax; the clinic says the fax log shows it sent. Both are probably telling the truth, which suggests the failure sits in the hand-off mechanism itself rather than in either team's diligence.

The coordinator started keeping a manual duplicate log, calling the hospital two days after every referral to confirm receipt. That closed the visibility gap for the patients she personally tracked, but it does not scale past the roughly forty referrals she can call in a week, and referral volume runs closer to ninety. The open question the team keeps circling back to is whether the fix belongs at the sending end, the receiving end, or in the handoff format itself, since a phone call that works for forty referrals a week is not a process, it is a workaround standing in for a missing one.
